_comment: EdgeCDSS — CONCENTRATION MASTER LIST. The inventory of record.
This file answers one question: what is in the bag? No clinical guideline
knows that, which is why concentrations live here and not in
drug_contracts.json. A milligram dose is a clinical claim; a millilitre
volume is a claim about this vial.
NOTHING HERE IS SIGNED. Every presentation ships signoff:false, so the
system serves milligram doses and no volumes at all until a clinician
signs. That is deliberate: it ends the 2.5x succinylcholine volume error
on merge rather than on signature.
A presentation is declared the way the vial is LABELLED — mass_mg and
volume_ml — and concentration_mg_ml is derived from them. The loader
refuses any presentation where the two disagree, which is what catches a
transcription slip.
TO SIGN: use set_concentration.py, which validates, logs the change and
refuses to sign anything it would reject. Editing this file by hand works
too, and the loader will detect and log the change on next import — but
the tool is the path that cannot get the guardrails wrong.
TO REVOKE: set signoff false. That needs no signature. Revoking is always
safe because it degrades to mg-only; declaring is what needs authority.
confirm_required: true means ALWAYS ask which vial, even if only one is
declared. Set it where guessing wrong is expensive.

guardrails._note: Tier 1 is structural: a value outside the absolute range is a unit error, not a vial. Tier 2 compares against the strengths the approved sources cite for that drug in drug_contracts.json forms[] — a declaration more than 10x away from every one of them is refused, because that is the shape of a decimal slip. Drugs no approved source lists (rocuronium) get tier 1 only, and are marked NO_SOURCED_STRENGTH so the weaker protection is visible rather than assumed.

entries.confirm_reason: Both presentations are common and they differ five-fold. The owner set this drug to always ask rather than assume, because a wrong guess here is a 5x error on an induction agent.

NOT ON THE WHO EML and absent from NASEMSO v3.0 — neither approved source cites a rocuronium strength, so this declaration has no source corroboration and the order-of-magnitude guardrail cannot protect it.
presentations.justification: Owner declaration: 100 mg/10 mL is the standard stocked presentation. Accepted with justification because no approved source lists rocuronium at all; this is the least-corroborated entry in the list.
